[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 1. Purpose]
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

[Purchase Policy › 4. Cost centres and budgets]
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

D_chunks.heading: [Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
D_chunks.text:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 5. Approval limits]
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT , not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.

D_chunks.heading: [Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
D_chunks.text:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 6. Supplier qualification]
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

D_chunks.heading: [Purchase Policy › 7. Prices]
D_chunks.text:
[Purchase Policy · POL-PUR-001 · v4.1 · effective 2026-04-01]
[Purchase Policy › 7. Prices]
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.

How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.

What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process

What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy

market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section

Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
